title: Planning
core_thesis: Trajectory planning bridges the gap between spatial intent and physical execution by producing time-parameterized contracts that respect kinematic feasibility, strict tail-latency budgeting, and derivative continuity at replacement seams.
pedagogical_strengths: Successfully grounds abstract latency constraints into tangible physical consequences, such as infinite acceleration demands causing motor current saturation.
Clearly distinguishes geometric spatial paths from time-parameterized trajectories, emphasizing the necessity of the uncompromising clock in physical AI systems.

student_friction_points.point: The dense mathematical notation for extreme mission tail quantile ($Q_{1-\epsilon_{\mathrm{mission}}/K}(L)$) is introduced abruptly in the takeaways without prior progressive disclosure or intuitive grounding in the main text.
How do we map the highly variable, probabilistic inference latencies of modern diffusion policies to the strict deterministic tail-latency budgets ($P_{99.99997}$) demanded by the hardware?

established_budgets_and_laws: Latency Budgeting: Action chunk horizon $H$ must strictly exceed the extreme tail replacement latency of the compute pipeline to prevent physical starvation.
Kinematic Continuity Law: Boundary derivatives must match exactly across plan seams ($\Delta \dot{\mathbf{q}} = 0$) to prevent infinite instantaneous acceleration and current loop saturation.
Terminal Stopping Budget: Every trajectory must conclude with a physically achievable stopping suffix sized by $T_{\text{stop}} \ge v_{\text{bound}}/a_{\text{dec}}$.
exported_concepts: Time-parameterized action chunks and kinodynamic trajectories
Seam lateness and boundary condition matching

surgical_edits.target_text: The physical machine executes voltage, current, and torque commands. It consumes voltage, current, and torque commands indexed against an uncompromising clock.
surgical_edits.improved_text: The physical machine executes voltage, current, and torque commands, consuming them strictly indexed against an uncompromising clock.

surgical_edits.target_text: A replacement trajectory will arrive late. Building on the causal boundary established in @sec-boundary-causal-boundary, treating that delay as an asynchronous communication error or a generic software exception shifts responsibility away from the trajectory generator to software layers that lack physical state context.
surgical_edits.improved_text: Because inference latency is variable, replacement trajectories will inevitably arrive late. Treating this delay as a generic software exception violates the causal boundary (@sec-boundary-causal-boundary), improperly shifting responsibility to system layers lacking the physical state context needed to safely halt the machine.

open_thematic_threads_for_part: How do the low-level hardware controllers and power electronics physically realize the high-frequency feedforward torques, and what happens when unmodeled environmental disturbances violate the planner's physical assumptions?
